title: Banked Memories for Soft SIMT Processors
problem: Soft SIMT processors on FPGAs require memory systems delivering high bandwidth (16+ ports) while maintaining high clock speeds (770+ MHz), but the design trade-offs between simpler multi-port and complex banked memory architectures are not well characterized.
motivation: As soft GPGPU architectures become practical on modern FPGAs with small footprints and high performance, optimizing the memory subsystem is critical for overall system performance and efficient resource utilization.
method: The authors built and tested 9 memory designs on FPGAs: some with multiple ports (simpler, supporting many simultaneous accesses) and others using banks (splitting memory into independent sections). They ran 51 benchmarks combining matrix transposition and FFT algorithms at different data sizes, measuring each design's speed, clock frequency (targeting 770+ MHz), and FPGA memory usage to see which works best when.
key_novelty: Simpler multi-port memories perform better on small datasets despite higher memory overhead, while banked memories become more efficient at larger data sizes.
contributions: Design and implementation of 9 memory architecture variants for FPGA-based soft SIMT processors
Benchmark suite of 51 tests combining memory-intensive (matrix transpose) and balanced (FFT) workloads
Quantitative trade-off analysis between multi-port and banked designs across bandwidth, frequency, and density
Design guidance for memory architecture selection based on dataset size and application needs

metrics.speedup: varies by architecture and dataset size
metrics.other: bandwidth up to 16 ports, Fmax >770 MHz, memory block utilization

limitations: Evaluation limited to matrix transposition and FFT benchmarks; generalizability to other memory access patterns and application domains not discussed.
primary_theme: FPGA memory architecture design for soft processors
